selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
selected_evidence.summary: Created and validated the sudoers drop-in and log file, then showed log entries with timestamp, user (root and testsudo), host, and full command for multiple sudo invocations.

selected_evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: grep against /var/log/secure and journalctl for the logged commands returned zero matches, both before and after the reboot, confirming sudo's syslog output was suppressed via !syslog.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (f43afa1c-4877-4ace-a101-d6bb0cd6ce3d), validated sudoers, and confirmed the log file was populated and correctly permissioned.
systemctl reboot was launched via a backgrounded sleep+reboot wrapper so the exec call returned successfully (pid captured) before the node dropped.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection timeout) immediately after reboot, then returned with a new boot_id (8c353e7c-f12f-4af6-8a18-9da9f178b5b5), distinct from the baseline, proving an actual restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging and continued exclusion from general log
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers config re-validated OK, log file and permissions persisted, a new sudo whoami command was correctly appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and journalctl showed zero matching entries for it.
